    92  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    93  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    94  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    95  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    96  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    97  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    98  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    99      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
   100      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
   101      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   102    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) accepted
   103    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

   110    --verified          Check in the mode the soundness theorem covers (default)
   111    --trusted           Skip the checks only the proof needs; outside the theorem
   112    --jobs=N            Worker threads (default: one per hardware thread, at most 16)
   113    --progress[=PACE]   Report progress on stderr: PACE is N declarations
   114                        (default 1), P% of each phase, or Ss seconds
   115    --pins FILE         Testing only: check with this Nat pin list instead of

   119    --                  End of options
   120

   122    --olean             Read modules and their import closure from .olean files
   123    --search-path=DIRS  Colon-separated .olean directories; repeatable
   124    --constant=NAME     Check only NAME and what it mentions; repeatable
   125  
   126  Exit status:
   127    0  accepted
   128    1  rejected: a declaration is invalid
   129    2  declined: an unsupported feature
   130    3  error: bad usage, malformed input or an internal failure

   133    README.md and OVERVIEW.md of the con-ron repository";

   618  pub fn render(n: &Name) -> Vec<u32> {
   619      match &n.0.kind {
   620          NameKind::Anonymous => {
   621              const A: [u32; 11] = [91, 97, 110, 111, 110, 121, 109, 111, 117, 115, 93];
   622              crate::kernel::core_types::code_points(&A)
   623          }
   624          _ => {
   625              let cs = component_list(n, Vec::new());
   626              let k = cs.len();
   627              display_acc_finish(render_from(&cs, k, display_acc_empty()))
   628          }
   629      }
   630  }

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L14-L85
    14  /-!
    15  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    16  
    17  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    18  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    19  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    20  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's headline theorems:
    21  
    22  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — the environment of every stream the Aeneas
    23    model of the Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    24  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    25    type `False` is never accepted by it;
    26  * `no_False_oleans` / `model_exists_oleans` — the same on `--olean`.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as their dependency closure, and §5's census prints their
    30  axioms.  What they assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    31  
    32  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    33  
    34  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    35  around the extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    36  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    37  
    38      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    39        → prepare_d → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the check phase)
    40  
    41  **The check phase is the one the binary's driver runs, pool and all**
    42  (`driver::check_decls_driver`): it builds the stream's index from the records
    43  (`stream_index::build_index`), freezes the tier with the index in it
    44  (`checker::freeze_tier`), runs every record's job on `pool::parallel_all`, and
    45  thaws the tier.  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` the index, `h7`
    46  the freeze, `h8` the pool), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    47  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  `h8` is the contract of the generic
    48  combinator `pool::parallel_all` at the driver's two verified closures (`ParallelAll`
    49  at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, each in increasing
    50  order, and for each a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`,
    51  accepting.  That contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    52  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    53  
    54  The proof:
    55  
    56  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s `…_refines` lemmas walk the Rust runs
    57     into twin runs from the twin's own start state `AState.init EStore.empty`,
    58     related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/`AStateInv`: lockstep); `rust_stages`;
    59  2. **Theorem 1** — `Bridge/Stages.lean` takes the twin runs:
    60     `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` makes the check phase's accept con-leche's pure
    61     fold `checkDeclsPure` accepting the denoted stream at `streamEnv` of it;
    62  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a model,
    63     and `no_proof_of_False_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream.
    64  
    65  ## The named hypotheses
    66  
    67  The headlines start from the binary's own start values (`startState` =
    68  `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`) and name the call the
    69  binary makes at each step.  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    70  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    71  they assume is exactly:
    72  
    73  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks: the binary
    74    parses with the verified reader loop `parse_source` over the driver's file
    75    handle, and `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
    76    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands out
    77    the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam;
    78  * on `--olean`, `hsnap : SnapshotOf finst fsv F` — the file instance answers as
    79    one snapshot `F`.
    80  
    81  `hpins` is the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list is what the verified
    82  decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems hold at every pin list);
    83  `model_exists_embedded` / `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded
    84  `PINS_TEXT`.
    85  -/

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L441-L445
   441  def RustDenotes (ds : alloc.vec.Vec arena.env.IDeclaration) (st : arena.monad.AState)
   442      (env : ConLeche.Env) : Prop :=
   443    ∃ (lst : ConRon.Arena.AState) (dsP : List ConLeche.Declaration),
   444      AStateRel emptyTier st lst ∧ ConRon.Bridge.denoteDecls lst.store (absIDeclL ds) = some dsP ∧
   445        env = ConLeche.Cached.streamEnv dsP

   329      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   330      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   331      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   332      let mut st = AState::empty();
   333      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-6b).
   334      // The parse, the pin walk and the index build own their own — the store is
   335      // owned (not frozen) — so what they are handed here is the EMPTY tier; the
   336      // check phase freezes the store's tier, the index with it, into a
   337      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker (`check_decls_driver`).
   338      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   339      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   340      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   341      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   342      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   343      // every job's bracket.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   344      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   345      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   346      // unlikely.
   347      // ConRon.Capstone: h1

    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    36    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    37    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    38        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

   184  structure SnapshotOf {Fs : Type} (inst : frontend.olean.files.OleanFs Fs) (fsv : Fs)
   185      (F : ConLeche.FS) : Prop where
   186    path_exists : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.path_exists fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   187      b = (F.real q).isSome
   188    real_path : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ r, inst.real_path fsv p = ok (.Ok r) →
   189      F.real q = some ⟨ConRon.Refine.absString r⟩ ∧ ConRon.Refine.StrWF r
   190    read_bin_file : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.read_bin_file fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   191      F.file q = some (absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b))
   192    read_range : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ off len b, inst.read_range fsv p off len = ok (.Ok b) →
   193      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b) =
   194        whole.extract off.val (min (off.val + len.val) whole.size)
   195    file_size : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ s, inst.file_size fsv p = ok (.Ok s) →
   196      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ s.val = whole.size

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3603-L3638
  3603  
  3604      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3605      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3606      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3607      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3608      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3609      ///
  3610      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3611      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3612      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3613      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3614      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3615      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3616      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3617      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3618      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3619      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3620      ///
  3621      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3622      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3623      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3624      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3625          match v {
  3626              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3627              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3628              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3629              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3630              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3631              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3632              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3633              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3634              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3635              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3636          }
  3637      }
  3638  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3888-L3935
  3888      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3889          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3890          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3891              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3892                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3893              } else {
  3894                  true
  3895              }
  3896          } else {
  3897              false
  3898          };
  3899          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3900              None
  3901          } else if pers.frozen {
  3902              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3903          } else {
  3904              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3905          };
  3906          match hit {
  3907              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3908              None => {
  3909                  if self.scratch_on {
  3910                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3911                      match at.1 {
  3912                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3913                          None => {
  3914                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3915                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3916                              } else {
  3917                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3918                                  let h: EIdx =
  3919                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3920                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3921                                  Ok(h)
  3922                              }
  3923                          }
  3924                      }
  3925                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3926                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3927                  } else {
  3928                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3929                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3930                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3931                      Ok(h)
  3932                  }
  3933              }
  3934          }
  3935      }

 10827  /// con-leche: none — **a job's bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10828  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3984-3992 dropScratch` —
 10829  /// the twin's `dropScratch` on a store that STAYS frozen (task #98-FREEZE): the
 10830  /// caches flushed and the scratch tiers emptied, the flag untouched.  A
 10831  /// worker's store is frozen for its whole life, so between two jobs it is
 10832  /// frozen with an empty scratch tier where the twin's is scratch-off; nothing

 10842  /// memos cleared and the scratch tiers emptied, the flag untouched.
 10843  pub fn enter_record(st: &mut AState) {
 10844      st.memos.reset();
 10845      st.store.clear_scratch();
 10846  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L64-L87
    64  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
    65  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its worker reads the
    66  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Checker.lean`).
    67  /// **The persistent tier and the stream's index into a value**: the four
    68  /// persistent tables and the index move into one `PersTier` handed back
    69  /// `frozen`, for the workers to read (the index is the base `ifenv_find` reads
    70  /// below a job's own layer).  A pure MOVE: the store's scratch tiers and flags
    71  /// are untouched (a worker's store is its own, `worker_state`), and
    72  /// `thaw_tier` puts everything back where it was.  The driver's store is not
    73  /// read between the two.
    74  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore, ix: IStreamIndex) -> PersTier {
    75      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
    76      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
    77      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
    78      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
    79      PersTier {
    80          frozen: true,
    81          n,
    82          l,
    83          ls,
    84          e,
    85          env: ix,
    86      }
    87  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1217-L1269
  1217  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:365-373 EStore
  1218  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1219  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1220  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1221  /// expressible.
  1222  ///
  1223  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1224  /// phase A's setup append to, and ONE flag, `scratch_on`.  **A store is in
  1225  /// one of two states, and "frozen" and "scratch on" are the same thing** (task
  1226  /// #98-FREEZE):
  1227  ///
  1228  /// * **owned, scratch off** (the parse, the setup, between phase A's
  1229  ///   declaration brackets): read through the EMPTY stand-in tier
  1230  ///   (`PersTier::empty`, `frozen` false), so every persistent read and every
  1231  ///   append goes to the owned field;
  1232  /// * **frozen, scratch on** (inside a declaration bracket, and a phase-B
  1233  ///   worker for its whole life): the owned field is empty — `freeze` moved it
  1234  ///   into a `PersTier` whose `frozen` bit is set — and the store is read
  1235  ///   through that tier, so every persistent read goes to it; every append is
  1236  ///   a SCRATCH append, so no append can reach a frozen persistent tier, by
  1237  ///   construction and not by a guard.
  1238  ///
  1239  /// Which tables a persistent read goes to is therefore the READER's to say
  1240  /// (`frozen`), not the store's: the choice is made by a value that is fixed
  1241  /// for the whole of a bracket or a worker, whatever runs inside it.  `freeze`
  1242  /// hands out a frozen tier and turns the scratch tier on; `thaw` takes it back
  1243  /// and turns it off; `empty_frozen` is a worker's store.  Promotion — the one
  1244  /// writer of the persistent tier inside a bracket — writes the frozen tier
  1245  /// itself, through `&mut PersTier` (`PersTier::intern_*`).
  1246  ///
  1247  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1248  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1249  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1250  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1251  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1252  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1253  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1254  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1255  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1256  pub struct PersTier {
  1257      /// This is a frozen store's tier: a store read through it reads its
  1258      /// persistent tables HERE.  `false` only for the empty stand-in an owned
  1259      /// store is handed (`PersTier::empty`), which is never read.
  1260      pub frozen: bool,
  1261      pub n: NTables,
  1262      pub l: LTables,
  1263      pub ls: LsTables,
  1264      pub e: ETables,
  1265      /// The stream's index, the frozen base of every job's environment
  1266      /// (`arena::env`'s `IFEnv` note): `checker::freeze_tier` moves it here, so
  1267      /// every worker reads one by reference.  Empty in every other tier.
  1268      pub env: IStreamIndex,
  1269  }

   583  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:55-76 FEnv
   584  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Env.lean:232-241 IFEnv` — the environment
   585  /// with its `O(1)` index (DESIGN.md §8.3 lesson 13), over the frozen base of a

   587  ///
   588  /// **The environment has two tiers, like the store.**  An `IFEnv` is one LAYER:
   589  /// a job's own, empty until its record pushes.  The BASE is the stream's index
   590  /// (`arena::stream_index::IStreamIndex`), built once before any check and

   592  /// it by reference.  The layer's own entries are all visible (con-leche's local
   593  /// index has no counter); the base is read below the layer's two bounds,
   594  /// con-leche's `FBase.below` and `FBase.belowRec`, which live here because the
   595  /// base itself is shared.
   596  ///

   598  /// lever 1): the twin's row carries the constant itself, a shared value in Lean
   599  /// and a second deep copy in Rust.  Every writer keeps `idx` and `env.consts`
   600  /// in step (`ifenv_push`, `ifenv_push_temp`, `ifenv_pop_temp`) and
   601  /// `ifenv_find` reads `env.consts[s]`.  The table map `tbls` is built the same
   602  /// way: its row is the table's slot in `env.tables`.
   603  pub struct IFEnv {

   605      pub idx: HashMap<NIdx, u64>,
   606      pub tbls: HashMap<NIdx, u64>,

   608      pub base_below: u64,
   609      /// The base's tables are visible below this record position
   610      /// (`FBase.belowRec`).
   611      pub base_below_rec: u64,

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L466-L513
   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:402-404 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:190-192 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L308-L541
   308  
   309  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:224-376 checkMainG
   310  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:87-98 readInputG
   311  /// The driver's front matter: the prelude, the streaming parse, the
   312  /// preparation, the pin walk, the receipts, then the index, the check phase
   313  /// and the verdict.
   314  /// It is the Lean twin's `runPipelineIO` with the heartbeat and the receipts
   315  /// around it (`Arena/Main.lean`), and `con-ron`'s `check_main` with the
   316  /// handles in place of the trees.
   317  fn check_main(a: &Args, input: &Input) -> u8 {
   318      let t0 = Instant::now();
   319      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   320          "--verified"
   321      } else {
   322          "--trusted"
   323      };
   324      let mode = if a.verified {
   325          CheckMode::Verified
   326      } else {
   327          CheckMode::Trusted
   328      };
   329      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   330      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   331      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   332      let mut st = AState::empty();
   333      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-6b).
   334      // The parse, the pin walk and the index build own their own — the store is
   335      // owned (not frozen) — so what they are handed here is the EMPTY tier; the
   336      // check phase freezes the store's tier, the index with it, into a
   337      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker (`check_decls_driver`).
   338      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   339      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   340      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   341      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   342      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   343      // every job's bracket.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   344      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   345      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   346      // unlikely.
   347      // ConRon.Capstone: h1
   348      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   349          Ok(()) => (),
   350          Err(e) => {
   351              eprintln!(
   352                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   353                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   354                  mode_tag
   355              );
   356              return 3;
   357          }
   358      }
   359      // The heartbeat (`--progress`), and its first line: what the run reads.
   360      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(con_ron_core::frontend::pace::pace_dup(&a.progress), t0);
   361      hb.read_starts(&match input {
   362          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   363          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   364      });
   365      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   366      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   367      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   368          Ok(p) => p,
   369          Err((e, line)) => {
   370              let what = match classify(&e) {
   371                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   372                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   373                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   374              };
   375              eprintln!(
   376                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   377                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   378                  what, mode_tag
   379              );
   380              return 3;
   381          }
   382      };
   383      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   384      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   385      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   386      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   387      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   388      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   389      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   390      // The `.olean` path ends in the same records (task #142); no capstone
   391      // premise is about it yet (OVERVIEW.md).
   392      // An `--olean` run's theorems hold references to their values, which their
   393      // jobs read (`driver::olean_job`); what that needs comes back beside the
   394      // records (`OleanRead`), and of it the check keeps only the pins and the
   395      // values (below, after the preparation).
   396      let read: std::io::Result<Result<(Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>), (CheckError, u64)>> = match input {
   397          Input::Ndjson(file) => match driver::parse_export_stream_d(pers, &mut st, file, export_c::CHUNK_SIZE) {
   398              Err(e) => {
   399                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), e);
   400                  return 3;
   401              }
   402              Ok((r, _)) => Ok(r.map(|p: ParseResultD| (p.decls, None))),
   403          },
   404          Input::Oleans(req) => Ok(con_ron::olean_fs::read_request(pers, &mut st, req, &a.progress)
   405              .map(|mut rd| (std::mem::take(&mut rd.decls), Some(rd)))),
   406      };
   407      let label: String = match input {
   408          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   409          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   410      };
   411      let (parsed_decls, olean): (Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>) = match read {
   412          Err(_) => return 3,
   413          Ok(Err((e, line))) => match classify(&e) {
   414              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   415                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   416                  return 2;
   417              }
   418              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   419              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   420              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   421                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   422                  return 1;
   423              }
   424              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   425                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", label, line, msg);
   426                  return 3;
   427              }
   428          },
   429          Ok(Ok(r)) => r,
   430      };
   431      let file_records = parsed_decls.len();
   432      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   433      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   434      // produced indexes into it.
   435      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   436      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   437      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   438      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   439      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   440      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   441      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   442      // What a record mentions, for the ground hoist: its expressions say it,
   443      // except a theorem's read from an `.olean`, whose load read it off the
   444      // file (con-leche's `usedOf`).
   445      let prepared = match match &olean {
   446          None => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, &DeclUsedConsts),
   447          Some(rd) => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, rd),
   448      } {
   449          Ok(p) => p,
   450          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   451      };
   452      // **What the check keeps of the read** (con-leche's `checkOleansG` takes
   453      // `rd.values`): the reader's pins and the values' modules.  The merged
   454      // constants, whose last reader is the preparation (`OleanRead.thmUses`), go
   455      // here, before the pool: on Mathlib that is 0.8 M constants and their
   456      // `uses` (DESIGN, task #145).
   457      let olean: Option<(OleanPins, Vec<ModRef>)> =
   458          olean.map(|rd| (rd.pins, rd.values));
   459      // the ground hoist's receipt
   460      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   461          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   462              .hoisted
   463              .iter()
   464              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   465              .collect();
   466          eprintln!(
   467              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   468               they ground: {}",
   469              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   470              names.join(", ")
   471          );
   472      }
   473      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   474      // outside the theorems)
   475      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   476          Ok(p) => p,
   477          Err(e) => {
   478              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   479              return 3;
   480          }
   481      };
   482      // What the parse line reports, printed once the index is built.
   483      hb.file_records = file_records;
   484      hb.synthesised = prepared.synthesised;
   485      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   486      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   487      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   488      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   489      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   490      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   491      // ConRon.Capstone: h5
   492      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins) {
   493          Ok(p) => p,
   494          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   495      };
   496      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   497      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`: the index, the frozen tier, and the pool
   498      // for the check phase).
   499      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   500          Some(n) => n,
   501          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   502      };
   503      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what builds and freezes the
   504      // index and the check phase is the pool at every worker count, so a run
   505      // with no heartbeat is the same computation as a run with one.
   506      // ConRon.Capstone: the index, the freeze and the pool (the driver's steps,
   507      // either observer)
   508      let on = con_ron_core::frontend::pace::pace_on(&a.progress);
   509      let ds = &prepared.decls;
   510      let verdict = match (&olean, input) {
   511          (Some((pk, values)), Input::Oleans(req)) => {
   512              let sp = &req.search_path;
   513              let job = |tier: &PersTier, w: &mut AState, c: &mut ValueCache, k: u64| {
   514                  driver::olean_job(tier, w, c, &mode, &ipins, ds, pk, values, sp, k)
   515              };
   516              if on {
   517                  driver::check_decls_driver_with(pers, &mut st, ds, jobs, &mut hb, value_cache_empty, job)
   518              } else {
   519                  driver::check_decls_driver_with(pers, &mut st, ds, jobs, &mut driver::Silent, value_cache_empty, job)
   520              }
   521          }
   522          _ => {
   523              if on {
   524                  driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, ds, jobs, &mut hb)
   525              } else {
   526                  driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, ds, jobs, &mut driver::Silent)
   527              }
   528          }
   529      };
   530      // **The headline number is the FILE's declaration-record count**: the
   531      // records the PARSE produced, which are the file's own.  Nothing the
   532      // preparation does moves it.
   533      let stream_records = file_records as u64;
   534      let code = match &verdict {
   535          Ok(_) => driver::verdict_accept(stream_records, mode_tag),
   536          Err((e, i)) => {
   537              driver::verdict_failure(pers, &st.store, &prepared.decls, e, *i, mode_tag, t0)
   538          }
   539      };
   540      exit_after_verdict(code)
   541  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-two names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

   160  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/NatOpPins.lean:75-78 _
   161  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Basis.lean:39-45 BasisKind.decls
   162  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:124-153 internAllPins` — **the
   163  /// one-time tree walk of DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d**: every datum the checker compares
   164  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —
   165  /// which, at the driver's call, is the persistent one.
   166  ///
   167  /// The five basis blocks' pins (what a basis block's and a quotient record's
   168  /// job compares the record with), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
   169  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose
   170  /// interned form is the checker's pin-list parameter (con-leche's task #304).
   171  pub fn intern_all_pins(
   172      pers: &PersTier,
   173      st: &mut AState,
   174      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
   175  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {
   176      match intern_all_basis(pers, st, 0) {
   177          Err(e) => Err(e),
   178          Ok(()) => match intern_all_axiom_pins(pers, st) {
   179              Err(e) => Err(e),
   180              Ok(()) => match intern_all_names(st) {
   181                  Err(e) => Err(e),
   182                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   183              },
   184          },
   185      }
   186  }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L907-L948
   907  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   908  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   909  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   910  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   911  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   912  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   913  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   914  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   915      /// The open reader.
   916      pub h: &'a mut R,
   917      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   918      pub chunk: usize,
   919      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   920      pub chunks: u64,
   921      /// The first read failure, if any.
   922      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   923  }
   924  
   925  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   926  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   927      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   928      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   929      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   930          if self.err.is_some() {
   931              return Vec::new();
   932          }
   933          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   934          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   935              Ok(n) => {
   936                  buf.truncate(n);
   937                  if n > 0 {
   938                      self.chunks += 1;
   939                  }
   940                  buf
   941              }
   942              Err(e) => {
   943                  self.err = Some(e);
   944                  Vec::new()
   945              }
   946          }
   947      }
   948  }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L589-L639
   589  pub fn olean_job(
   590      tier: &PersTier,
   591      w: &mut AState,
   592      cache: &mut con_ron_core::frontend::olean::records::ValueCache,
   593      mode: &CheckMode,
   594      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   595      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   596      pk: &con_ron_core::frontend::olean::spec::OleanPins,
   597      values: &Vec<con_ron_core::frontend::olean::records::ModRef>,
   598      sp: &Vec<Vec<u32>>,
   599      k: u64,
   600  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> {
   601      let d = match ds.get(k as usize) {
   602          Some(d) => d,
   603          None => return checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, ds, k),
   604      };
   605      let code: Option<u64> = match d {
   606          // a theorem's value is a reference only if its handle is a `bvar`: the store's
   607          // projection reads the bvar table at the handle's slot whatever its tag
   608          IDeclaration::ThmDecl(_, v) if v.tag() == con_ron_core::arena::handle::ETAG_BVAR => {
   609              w.store.view_bvar(tier, v)
   610          }
   611          _ => None,
   612      };
   613      match (code, d) {
   614          (Some(code), IDeclaration::ThmDecl(cv, _)) => {
   615              con_ron_core::arena::core::enter_record(w);
   616              let r = match con_ron_core::frontend::olean::records::read_value(
   617                  &crate::olean_fs::StdFs,
   618                  pk,
   619                  tier,
   620                  &mut w.store,
   621                  sp,
   622                  values,
   623                  cache,
   624                  code,
   625              ) {
   626                  Err(e) => Err((e, k)),
   627                  Ok(v) => {
   628                      let pd = IDeclaration::ThmDecl(ienv::i_constant_val_dup(cv), v);
   629                      match stream_index::record_check(tier, w, mode, pins, k, &pd) {
   630                          Err(e) => Err((e, k)),
   631                          Ok(()) => Ok(()),
   632                      }
   633                  }
   634              };
   635              con_ron_core::arena::core::leave_record(w);
   636              r
   637          }
   638          _ => checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, ds, k),
   639      }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L516-L576
   516  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:224-376 checkMainG
   517  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:152-169 checkOleansG
   518  /// `check_decls_driver` with a worker state of the caller's beside each
   519  /// worker's `AState` (`init_x`, one per worker) and the caller's job: an
   520  /// `--olean` run's workers keep the module region they read a theorem's value
   521  /// from (`olean_job`, con-leche's `OleanWorker`), every other run's job is
   522  /// `checker::run_job` with nothing beside it.
   523  pub fn check_decls_driver_with<O, X, I, J>(
   524      pers: &PersTier,
   525      st: &mut AState,
   526      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   527      jobs: u64,
   528      obs: &mut O,
   529      init_x: I,
   530      job: J,
   531  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)>
   532  where
   533      O: PhaseObserver + Send,
   534      I: Fn() -> X + Sync,
   535      J: Fn(&PersTier, &mut AState, &mut X, u64) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> + Sync,
   536  {
   537      // THE INDEX (the last step of the parse phase): every record's constants and
   538      // tables, a name's first entry winning, read off the records alone.
   539      obs.index_starts();
   540      let ix: IStreamIndex = stream_index::build_index(pers, st, stream_index::stream_index_empty(), ds, 0)?;
   541      obs.parse_done(pers, &st.store, ds.len());
   542      let m = ds.len();
   543      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   544      obs.check_starts(m, workers);
   545      // THE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and become
   546      // a value every worker reads.  `st` keeps its (empty) store, its tables
   547      // moved out, so the observer can still read a label back through the tier.
   548      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, ix);
   549      // THE CHECK PHASE: the job at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   550      // folding it over the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and
   551      // the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs`.
   552      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   553      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   554      let r = parallel_all(
   555          m,
   556          workers,
   557          || (checker::worker_state(&st.pins), init_x()),
   558          |w: &mut (AState, X), k| job(&tier, &mut w.0, &mut w.1, k as u64),
   559          |w: &(AState, X), k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, &w.0, m, ds, k),
   560      );
   561      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   562          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   563          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   564      };
   565      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the check — the verdict line's
   566      // declaration label, the failing record's name — reads a handle back out of
   567      // `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has gone out of scope
   568      // answers `None` to every one of them.
   569      let _ix: IStreamIndex = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   570      let v = pool_verdict(r);
   571      obs.check_done(m, match &v {
   572          Err((_, pos)) => Some(*pos),
   573          Ok(()) => None,
   574      });
   575      v
   576  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L35-L48
    35  //! ## What a worker is, in the check phase
    36  //!
    37  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what the check phase is: "the persistent tier is
    38  //! immutable, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**"
    39  //! (`record_job` is the bracket; nothing writes the persistent tier after the
    40  //! index is built and frozen, and a worker never holds it `&mut`).  So the
    41  //! driver's `init`
    42  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    43  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    44  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    45  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier`, which
    46  //! holds the stream's index.  A job reads it through an empty layer of its own
    47  //! at its record's view and pushes into that layer.  So a worker costs no
    48  //! environment copy at all.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L119-L131
   119  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:199-227 checkPool
   120  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:64-71 AState.worker` — the twin's
   121  /// worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   122  /// **A worker's start state** (the cited `init`): the empty store, FROZEN
   123  /// (`EStore::empty_frozen`, task #98-FREEZE), so that every persistent read goes
   124  /// to the `PersTier` the boundary froze and every append is a scratch append;
   125  /// fresh memos and caches; and a copy of the pins.  The store stays frozen for
   126  /// the worker's life: `record_job` only empties its scratch tier.
   127  pub fn worker_state(pins: &Pins) -> AState {
   128      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty_frozen());
   129      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);
   130      st
   131  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L232-L293
   232  
   233  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:457-483 parMapWorkersIO
   234  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:199-227 checkPool
   235  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   236  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   237  ///
   238  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker,
   239  /// > each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step` over its
   240  /// > claimed indices in claim order, which is increasing, and every step
   241  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   242  ///
   243  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   244  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   245  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   246  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   247  ///
   248  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   249  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   250  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   251  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   252  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   253  /// not depend on it.
   254  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   255      n: usize,
   256      workers: usize,
   257      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   258      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   259      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   260  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {
   261      let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
   262      let limit = AtomicUsize::new(n);
   263      let run = || worker(n, &next, &limit, &init, &step, &after);
   264      let mut results: Vec<Vec<(usize, Result<(), E>)>> = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   265      let mut panicked = false;
   266      std::thread::scope(|scope| {
   267          let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   268          for w in 0..workers {
   269              let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
   270                  .stack_size(STACK_BYTES)
   271                  .name(format!("check-{}", w))
   272                  .spawn_scoped(scope, &run);
   273              match spawned {
   274                  Ok(h) => handles.push(h),
   275                  // Out of threads, or out of address space for another stack:
   276                  // run on the workers already spawned (the module note).
   277                  Err(_) => break,
   278              }
   279          }
   280          if handles.is_empty() {
   281              results.push(run());
   282          }
   283          for h in handles {
   284              match h.join() {
   285                  Ok(rs) => results.push(rs),
   286                  Err(_) => panicked = true,
   287              }
   288          }
   289      });
   290      if panicked {
   291          return Err(ParallelError::Panicked);
   292      }
   293      first_failure(merge_results(n, results))

   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204

   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

   101  theorem Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge (V : Type w) [ConLeche.SetTheory V]
   102      {pins : List INatOpPinSet} {pinsP : List NatOpPinSet}
   103      {ds : Array IDeclaration} {dsP : List Declaration} {s s' : AState} {I : IStreamIndex}
   104      (hk : CoreSpec Arena.checkFuel) (hind : IndSpec)
   105      (hst : DriverOK s) (hoff : s.store.scratchOn = false)
   106      (hpersPins : PersPins s) (hpp : PersPinSets pins) (hpins : PinsDenote s.store pins pinsP)
   107      (hpd : ∀ x ∈ ds.toList, PersDecl x) (hden : denoteDecls s.store ds.toList = some dsP)
   108      (hrun : Arena.PooledAccepts .verified pins ds s I s') :

   110        = .ok (ConLeche.Cached.streamEnv dsP) := by

   112    obtain ⟨hst', hx, hp', -, hI, hpI⟩ := buildIndex_run constsSpec tablesSpec hst hoff hpd hden hidx
   113    have hx' := PExt.of_ext hx

   116        Frontend.denoteDecl s'.store ds[i] = some dsP[i] := fun i hi => by

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/
    73  @[expose] def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Rel.lean#L59-L76
    59  /-! ## The core grade -/
    60  
    61  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    62  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    63  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    64  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    65  theorem PStep.toCore {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    66      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK false env fe s) : CoreStep env fe s s' :=
    67    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩

    70  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    71  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    72  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/
    73  @[expose] def CSpec (env : Env) (fe : IFEnv) {α : Type}
    74      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=

    76      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L127-L173
   127  /-! ## The spines -/
   128  
   129  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   130  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   131  
   132  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   133  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   134  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   135  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   136  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   137      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   138      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   139        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   140    intro n
   141    induction n with
   142    | zero =>
   143      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   144      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   145      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   146      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   147    | succ n ih =>
   148      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   149      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   150      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   151      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   152      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   153      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   154      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   155      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   156      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   157          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   158            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   159        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   160        congr 1
   161        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   162        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   163        congr 1
   164        omega
   165      rw [hkey]
   166      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   167  
   168  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   169      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   170    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   171    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   172    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   173    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L633-L645
   633  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   634  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   635  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   636  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   637      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   638      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   639    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   640  
   641  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   642  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   643      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   644      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   645    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

   615      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}
   616        (fuel : Std.U64) (args : alloc.vec.Vec arena.handle.EIdx) (i : Std.Usize) (t : Std.U64) (e : arena.handle.EIdx),
